layers.basics: RF amplifiers boost weak antenna signals (LNAs) or drive antennas (power amplifiers) with matching networks at both ends.
layers.deeper: LNAs trade low noise figure for gain; PAs trade efficiency for linearity (Class AB, Doherty).
layers.expert: Stability factors K and Δ; noise figure circles; 1-dB compression, IP3; PA efficiency η=P_out/P_DC; envelope tracking.

title: S-parameters
summary: Reflection and transmission of waves at ports.

layers.basics: S-parameters describe how much of a wave entering a port reflects or passes through to another, measured with a network analyzer.
layers.deeper: S11 is input reflection (match), S21 is gain or insertion loss.
layers.expert: b=S a with reference impedance Z₀=50 Ω; cascade via T-parameters; passivity |S|≤1; de-embedding fixtures; Touchstone file format.

layers.basics: A mixer multiplies two signals, producing sum and difference frequencies that shift a band to a different carrier; filters pick the wanted band.
layers.deeper: Superheterodyne receivers mix down to a fixed IF where filtering is easy; image rejection matters.
layers.expert: Conversion gain, LO leakage, double-balanced Gilbert cell; SAW/BAW/ceramic filters in phones; direct-conversion and zero-IF issues (DC offset, I/Q mismatch).

title: VLSI digital CMOS design
summary: Billions of gates on one die.

layers.basics: VLSI design builds chips from standard cells synthesised from HDL, placed and routed by tools.
layers.deeper: Flow: RTL → logic synthesis → floorplan → place → clock tree → route → timing signoff → tape-out.
layers.expert: Power, performance, area (PPA) trade-offs; clock gating; multi-Vt cells; interconnect RC dominates delay; design-for-test (scan chains).

title: Analog IC design
summary: Amplifiers, references and converters on silicon.

layers.basics: Analog ICs use transistor matching and feedback to make precise circuits; layout symmetry is part of the design.
layers.deeper: Bandgap references, op-amps, PLLs, ADCs; gm/Id methodology.
layers.expert: Bandgap V_BG≈1.2 V = V_BE + k·V_T cancelling temperature; matching σ(ΔV_T)=A_VT/√(WL); noise/power/speed triangle.

title: IC layout and verification
summary: Drawing the masks and proving them right.

layers.basics: Layout draws the polygons of each mask; verification (DRC, LVS) checks rules and that layout matches the schematic.
layers.deeper: Parasitic extraction reveals resistances and capacitances that slow real chips.
layers.expert: Process design kit (PDK); antenna rule; electromigration and IR drop checks; OPC for lithography; formal equivalence; GDSII.

layers.basics: Light guided by total internal reflection in glass fibre carries most of the world’s long-distance data.
layers.deeper: Single-mode fibre has ~0.2 dB/km loss at 1550 nm; erbium amplifiers and wavelength-division multiplexing raise capacity.
layers.expert: Core 9 µm; dispersion D≈17 ps/(nm·km); coherent detection and DSP compensate impairments; capacity limits near Shannon (~100 Tb/s per fibre).

title: Photonics and lasers
summary: Using light for signals and sensing.

layers.basics: Photonic chips guide light on silicon for data links and sensors; lasers provide coherent sources.
layers.deeper: Silicon photonics reuses CMOS fabs; modulators, waveguides, ring resonators, Ge photodetectors.
layers.expert: Mach–Zehnder modulator V_π; ring resonator FSR=λ²/(n_g L); co-packaged optics for datacentres; LiDAR with FMCW.

open_questions: Can on-chip lasers be integrated cheaply in silicon at scale?

title: Wireless communications: 5G and 6G

layers.basics: 5G uses wider bandwidths, millimetre waves and massive antenna arrays; 6G research aims at sub-THz bands and AI-native networks.
layers.deeper: NR air interface uses OFDM with flexible numerology; slicing and edge computing serve latency-sensitive services.
layers.expert: 5G NR: 410 MHz–7.125 GHz (FR1) and 24–52 GHz (FR2); 6G targets (≈2030) not yet standardised: THz links, integrated sensing and communication, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces.

open_questions: Which 6G spectrum and architecture will be standardised?

layers.basics: Using several antennas at both ends sends parallel data streams over the same spectrum.
layers.deeper: Capacity grows roughly with min(Nt,Nr) in rich scattering; beamforming focuses energy on users.
layers.expert: SVD of channel H splits into parallel eigenchannels; C=Σlog₂(1+σᵢ²P/N₀); massive MIMO exploits channel hardening; precoding (ZF, MMSE).

layers.basics: Radar sends a pulse and measures the echo’s delay (range) and Doppler shift (speed).
layers.deeper: Radar equation gives detection range; pulse compression improves resolution; automotive radars use FMCW at 77 GHz.
layers.expert: R=cτ/2; Doppler f_d=2v/λ; P_r=P_tG²λ²σ/((4π)³R⁴); CFAR detection; synthetic aperture imaging.

title: Robotics and mechatronics
summary: Machines that sense, think and move.

layers.basics: Robots combine sensors, actuators, electronics and control software.
layers.deeper: Kinematics, motor control, sensor fusion, path planning.
layers.expert: Jacobian-based inverse kinematics; SLAM; trajectory optimisation; torque control and impedance control.

title: Machine learning and AI for engineers

layers.basics: ML fits models to data; engineers use it for signal classification, predictive maintenance and control.
layers.deeper: Regression, classification, neural networks, training by gradient descent; careful validation avoids overfitting.
layers.expert: Backpropagation; CNNs/transformers; quantisation to int8; edge AI on microcontrollers (TinyML); data-centre accelerators dominated by matrix multiply energy.

layers.basics: GPUs, TPUs and NPUs have thousands of multiply–accumulate units and wide memory links to run neural networks efficiently.
layers.deeper: Energy is dominated by moving data, not arithmetic; systolic arrays minimise it.
layers.expert: Roofline model; int8/FP8 formats; HBM bandwidth ~1–3 TB/s; sparsity; in-memory computing proposals.

layers.basics: Images are 2D arrays; filters blur, sharpen and find edges; video exploits similarity between frames.
layers.deeper: JPEG uses the DCT; H.264/AV1 add motion compensation.
layers.expert: 2D convolution and separable kernels; demosaicing; Canny edges; DCT energy compaction; rate–distortion.

layers.basics: Electrodes pick up microvolt-to-millivolt signals from heart and brain; amplifiers must reject mains hum and motion noise.
layers.deeper: ECG ~1 mV, EEG ~10–100 µV; differential amplification, filtering 0.05–150 Hz, isolation for safety.
layers.expert: Right-leg drive reduces common-mode; electrode half-cell potentials; patient leakage <10 µA; IEC 60601; pulse oximetry uses two wavelengths.

layers.basics: Devices like pacemakers, defibrillators, and MRI scanners rely on precise electronics under strict safety rules.
layers.deeper: Regulatory classes and risk analysis shape design; MRI uses RF coils and gradient amplifiers.
layers.expert: Defibrillator: ~200 J biphasic shock; pacemaker µW-level power for >10 years; MRI RF at 42.58 MHz/T for protons.

layers.basics: PV panels produce DC; inverters convert it to AC, and MPPT electronics extract the most power.
layers.deeper: Panel I–V curve has a knee; maximum power point shifts with light and temperature.
layers.expert: MPPT via perturb-and-observe; module efficiency 20–24%; PR (performance ratio); string vs micro-inverters; bypass diodes.

title: Wind energy

layers.basics: Wind turns blades connected to a generator; power electronics adapt variable speed to a fixed grid frequency.
layers.deeper: Power ∝ v³; Betz limit 59% of wind’s kinetic power.
layers.expert: P=½ρAv³C_p; DFIG vs full-converter machines; pitch control; capacity factors 30–55% offshore.

formula: P = ½ ρ A v³ C_p

layers.basics: Batteries store energy chemically; battery management systems keep cells within safe voltage, current and temperature.
layers.deeper: Li-ion energy density ~150–270 Wh/kg; cycle life 1000–5000; state-of-charge estimation by coulomb counting and Kalman filters.
layers.expert: Equivalent-circuit (Thevenin) models; thermal runaway; sodium-ion and solid-state developments; grid storage economics.

layers.basics: An EV has a battery pack, inverter and motor; the inverter controls torque, and braking recovers energy.
layers.deeper: Permanent-magnet synchronous motors with field-oriented control; 400 V or 800 V pack architectures.
layers.expert: Efficiency maps; SiC inverters cut losses ~70% vs Si IGBTs; onboard charger and DC fast charging (CCS ≤350 kW); thermal management.

layers.basics: MEMS are tiny mechanical structures etched in silicon that sense motion, pressure or sound, such as phone accelerometers and microphones.
layers.deeper: A proof mass on springs shifts a capacitance when accelerated; readout electronics convert it to voltage.
layers.expert: Capacitive sensing ΔC/C; gyroscopes use Coriolis coupling between vibration modes; scaling laws favour surface forces; nanomaterials (graphene, nanowires, 2D semiconductors).

title: Quantum engineering and quantum computing hardware

layers.basics: Quantum computers use qubits (superconducting circuits, trapped ions, spins in silicon, photons) that can be in superpositions; hardware is cooled and shielded to preserve fragile states.
layers.deeper: Superconducting qubits operate at ~10 mK; gate fidelities of 99.5–99.9%; error correction needs thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit.
layers.expert: Coherence times T₁,T₂ from µs to ms (superconducting) to seconds (ions); surface codes with threshold ≈1%; scaling bottlenecks: wiring, cryo-electronics, fabrication yield.

open_questions: Which qubit platform will scale to fault-tolerant machines?
Can error-correction overhead be reduced enough for practical applications?

title: Computer networks and the Internet of Things

layers.basics: IoT devices sense and communicate over Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, LoRa or cellular, usually on batteries.
layers.deeper: Protocols such as MQTT, CoAP; trade-off between range, data rate and power.
layers.expert: LoRa sensitivity −137 dBm; BLE connection events; over-the-air updates; edge computing; device identity and lifecycle management.

title: Hardware security

layers.basics: Chips can leak secrets through power use, timing or electromagnetic emissions; secure designs protect keys.
layers.deeper: Secure boot, hardware roots of trust, physically unclonable functions (PUFs), tamper resistance.
layers.expert: Side-channel attacks (DPA, timing), fault injection, Spectre-class microarchitectural leaks, hardware trojans, supply-chain verification.

open_questions: How can speculative-execution leaks be eliminated without large performance losses?
